input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there

doc_friction.issue: A log ending in my own 'DONE-EXIT 3' marker was not recognised as done (it wants 'DONE' followed by a space or 'DONE exit'); I switched to the 'DONE exit N' spelling the tool prints.

Started with run_in_background, it still detaches after 100 s (CLAUDECODE is set and stdout is not a tty), so the background task exits 3 and you must wait on a second log; --foreground is needed inside run_in_background.

notes: Critique mode: no agent-owned backlog item was open. Lens: the doc-friction table (measure --section 'doc friction'). Five 2026-11-12 reports said --for-changes left check_post_frontmatter UNRUN behind portfolio-pages' 300 s site-builder suite. Fixes in run_workflow_locally.py: (1) job_order runs jobs in needs: order, lowest timeout-minutes first, so build (20 min) runs before test (30 min); (2) false_on_pull_request skips steps and jobs whose if: cannot hold on a pull request (&& chains with a github.event_name term only). That also removed a 10-minute hang in 'Add the development dashboard', which waited for a file from a skipped background step; I found the hang while checking the new order end to end. Verification: test_run_workflow_locally passes 140 tests (5 new); main_health 58/58 green before the change. In a by-name portfolio-pages run (--foreground) the front-matter check passed at 0.2 s, the build job finished in about 9 s, and the whole run took about 100 s. The site-builder suite failed 164 of 1577 tests in this container. Another run today reported the same container-only failure (171 of 1572), and this diff does not touch platform/pages, so CI's test job is the judge. Metric for a later Verify: doc_friction entries saying a cheap check went UNRUN behind the site-builder suite, baseline 5 on 2026-11-12 before this change. No backlog ids touched (the backlog lives under gated /prompts/).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: diagnose the ordering fault from friction reports, two small runner changes with tests, end-to-end run, post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
